Suppose $f$ is continuous and strictly decreasing. Then $h(x) = f(x) - x$ is strictly decreasing. As $x \to -\infty$, $f(x) \to +\infty$ (since $f$ decreasing and onto) and $-x \to +\infty$, so $h(x) \to +\infty$. As $x \to +\infty$, $f(x) \to -\infty$ and $-x \to -\infty$, so $h(x) \to -\infty$. *On all of $\mathbb{R}$:* First verify $f \circ g = g \circ f$. For $x \in [a_n, a_{n+1}]$:
$$f(g(x)) = g^{n+1}(f(g^{-(n+1)}(g(x)))) = g^{n+1}(f(g^{-n}(x))) = g(g^n(f(g^{-n}(x)))) = g(f(x)).$$

Now for $x \in [a_n, a_{n+1}]$, using $f \circ g = g \circ f$ iteratively:
$$f(f(x)) = f\big(g^n(f(g^{-n}(x)))\big) = g^n\big(f(f(g^{-n}(x)))\big) = g^n\big(g(g^{-n}(x))\big) = g(x),$$
where the third equality uses $f \circ f = g$ on $[a_0, a_1]$ (since $g^{-n}(x) \in [a_0, a_1]$). ✓
